Tyras page: 'In 56 AD, it seems to have been restored by the Romans under Nero'; it then 'became part of the Roman province' of Lower Moesia (a unit of the Classis Flavia Moesica there) and 'Romans remained there until the end of the 4th century under Theodosius I'. The Roman Empire shapes of 68-215 draw this strip (29 cells in Odessa and Mykolayiv); the Sarmatian region of the Pontic steppe covers it, so the size rule had been giving it to the Sarmatians. Rome never held this land, so the counterpart is the Dacians (the page says the Iazyges took 'absolute control of the territory from the Dacians', c. 20 AD).

ledger.note: 375: the Huns break the Alans. 'In 375, the Huns conquered most of the Alans living to the east of the Don river'; Alans page 'invaded the Goths in 375 together with the Huns'; 'Some of the other Alans remained under the rule of the Huns'. The Iazyges were 'absorbed into the Huns' by Attila's time. Alans page: 'Around 370 ... the Huns attacked the Don Alans, killing many of them and establishing an alliance with the survivors', and 'Following the Hunnic invasion in 370, other Alans ... migrated westward'; the huns dossier (ledger 1) takes 370 and the string 'Alans of the Don (Pontic Alans)'. Both pages are cited; 375 is kept because the Sarmatians page, this dossier's main source, dates the conquest to 375.

notes: Revised after review (ia-01-x fix pass). New state (Cliopatria has no Sarmatians; its 'Alans' row 414-438 is the Iberian Alans, eu-06). The Sarmatians were tribal confederations (Iazyges, Roxolani, Aorsi, Siraces, Alans), not a state: one soft combined shape. START: the dossier now starts at 313 BC (was 200 BC), the year of the second Scythian defeat after which the page has the Sarmatians 'crossing the Don river and invading Scythia'; it mirrors four of scythia's six events that name 'sarmatians': 313 loss (gain here), 313 contest_start, 224 contest_end and 224 dissolve (gain here, moved from 200 BC). Scythia ledger 12 (-339 contest_start) and 13 (-313 contest_end) have no mirror here because they precede the start: the page says the Don was crossed only after both defeats, so ia-01-a should re-point them to the Sauromatians (the infobox's 'Preceded by', unwritten) or to nobody. REGION DISAGREEMENT: scythia's 313 loss draws Cliopatria's Scythia -404 minus -350 (1,560 cells, 'the steppe east of the Don'); of it, 724 cells lie on the Pontic steppe and are taken here, while 836 cells of forest-steppe (Voronezh, Kursk, Belgorod, Tambov, Lipetsk, Sumy, Chernihiv) are not on the Sarmatians page as Sarmatian land; ia-01-a should send that remainder to nobody. The 224 gain is scythia's own successor land (Scythia -225 minus Crimea, Kherson, Mykolayiv); the -100 keyframes onward still include Kherson and Mykolayiv, which scythia gives to the Scythian kingdom of Crimea (no page opened for it here). 113: the counterpart is now the Dacians, not Rome (Iazyges page: Trajan 'did not incorporate the steppe between the Tisza river and the Transylvanian mountains into the province of Dacia'); the roman-empire counterpart of the Sarmatian wars stays. 375: the Sarmatians page (conquest of most Alans east of the Don) says 375, the Alans page 'Around 370' (Hunnic attack on the Don Alans, alliance with the survivors); the huns dossier ledger 1 uses 370 and the string 'Alans of the Don (Pontic Alans)': the huns owner should use the slug sarmatians and either year; this dossier keeps 375. 207 and 260 losses to Gothia use Cliopatria's Gothia shapes: the Sarmatians page says 'around 200' and 'the 3rd century', the Goths page gives the Chernyakhov culture 'from the Danube ... to the Don' by the mid-3rd century, no year. Crimea (the Scythian kingdom of Crimea, to 275 AD) is not drawn. The page gives no area, so no infobox ratio. After 375 the Alans of the north Caucasus continue to Alania (880 onward); the Iazyges end as part of the Huns. No ruler or capital is recorded. Gazetteer names used (North Caucasus, Lower Volga, Pontic Steppe, Crimea, Bessarabia, Crisana, Kecskemet, Debrecen, Kalmyk, Krasnodar) all resolve. Counterparts without dossiers: Dacians, the Sauromatians and the Scythian kingdom of Crimea.
